question: In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin intervene (n):
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Extracellular peptides" -> "transported into the cell" -> "processed by TAP proteins" -> "presented on MHC class I molecules" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Extracellular peptides" -> "processed in the endoplasmic reticulum" -> "tapasina assists in peptide loading" -> "peptides presented on MHC class I" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Extracellular peptides" -> "loaded onto MHC class II molecules" -> "HLA-DM facilitates peptide exchange" -> "effective antigen presentation" -> 92%
CHAIN: "Extracellular proteins" -> "degraded by proteasome" -> "produces peptides" -> "peptides presented on MHC class I" -> 88%
CHAIN: "Extracellular peptides" -> "bind to HLA-B molecules" -> "presented to CD8+ T cells" -> "immune response activation" -> 85%
analysis: Peptides of extracellular origin are typically processed and presented by MHC class II molecules, which involve the HLA-DM molecule in the loading of these peptides onto MHC class II. The TAP proteins and proteasome are more involved in the processing of intracellular peptides for MHC class I presentation. Therefore, the correct option that specifically relates to the processing and presentation of extracellular peptides is HLA-DM.
